projects.description:
The United Nations strengthened capacities of MSMEs, micro producers, cooperatives and women-led enterprises to expand market linkages and integrate into value chains.
Cultural entrepreneurs and artisans were supported to participate in multi-city events, national fairs and festivals, enhancing market visibility and regional linkages. In Taj Ganj, 100 artisans and youth were trained in cultural entrepreneurship to build sustainable tourism-linked enterprises.
Digital and institutional innovations advanced business mentoring and market access. The COMPASS digital platform connected women entrepreneurs with private-sector mentors, while a partnership with the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) promoted gender-responsive public procurement and expanded sourcing from women-led enterprises.
At the community level, 3,500 women smallholder farmers strengthened their capacities through rights awareness and cooperative-based livelihood models, supporting collective enterprise development and improved access to markets.

projects.description:
The United Nations strengthened institutional and financing mechanisms to improve women-led MSMEs’ access to affordable finance, digital capabilities and business support services.
Through the Fund for Women Entrepreneurs, an innovative blended financing model mobilised USD 1.3 million in low-cost, collateral-free credit from over 2,100 social investors, expanding access to capital for underserved women entrepreneurs. The initiative supported 2,619 women-led enterprises — 80% from SC, ST and OBC communities — with finance, mentoring and digital literacy, enhancing their capacity to improve business operations, adopt new models and scale sustainably.
With a 96% repayment rate and 4,071 jobs created, the model demonstrated a scalable and inclusive approach to strengthening women-led MSMEs and promoting equitable enterprise growth.

projects.description:
The United Nations strengthened policies, institutions and community systems to improve Female Labour Force Participation (FLFPR), advance gender parity and uphold rights at work.
Evidence-based advisory and financing analysis informed gender-responsive childcare models and revisions to national schemes, alongside pilot childcare centres that demonstrated affordable solutions to support women’s economic participation. Regional technical assistance built the capacities of over 390 stakeholders to design sustainable and inclusive care systems, while community skilling initiatives enabled women from low-income communities to access income-generating roles in the care economy.
Technical inputs to national and state task forces supported gender-responsive labour and employment policies, integrating care economy approaches to increase women’s workforce participation. The UN also supported the adoption of a State Plan of Action on child labour and integrated Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work — including elimination of child and forced labour — into industry training systems, promoting safer, more equitable employment across sectors.

projects.description:
The United Nations strengthened national and state skill ecosystem actors — including MSDE, NCVET, SSDMs, SSCs and industry bodies — to deliver gender-responsive, demand-driven and future-ready skilling systems. UN technical inputs informed the revision of the National Policy for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (2025), apprenticeship reforms, skill categorisation standards, and industry alignment through platforms such as FICCI and CII.
At the state level, district skill gap assessments in Jharkhand informed District and State Skill Development Plans, strengthening coordinated and data-driven planning. Nationally accredited digital, financial literacy and employability programmes reached over 1.4 million young people, with 52 per cent women, embedding 21st-century skills within government systems.
UN support advanced gender-responsive institutional reforms, with 74 institutions integrating employability, STEM and AI skills, and technical institutes adopting gender equality and POSH modules. Partnerships with 46 private sector companies expanded mentorship, apprenticeship and employment pathways, while targeted initiatives supported young women, marginalised youth and aspiring entrepreneurs to transition into decent work.

projects.description:
The United Nations strengthened capacities of MSMEs, micro producers, cooperatives and women-led enterprises to expand market linkages and integrate into value chains.
Cultural entrepreneurs and artisans were supported to participate in multi-city events, national fairs and festivals, enhancing market visibility and regional linkages. In Taj Ganj, 100 artisans and youth were trained in cultural entrepreneurship to build sustainable tourism-linked enterprises.
Digital and institutional innovations advanced business mentoring and market access. The COMPASS digital platform connected women entrepreneurs with private-sector mentors, while a partnership with the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) promoted gender-responsive public procurement and expanded sourcing from women-led enterprises.
At the community level, 3,500 women smallholder farmers strengthened their capacities through rights awareness and cooperative-based livelihood models, supporting collective enterprise development and improved access to markets.

children.description:
Indicator: Reduction in emission intensity of GDP-
- UNDP:  Supported the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change on realizing a reduction of over 4.9 million tonnes of CO2-equivalent emissions. This was accomplished through the implementation of climate-friendly alternatives, adapting to the phase-out of ozone-depleting substances in MSMEs within the Refrigeration and Air-conditioning (RAC) and Polyurethane (PU) foam manufacturing sector 

Indicator: Restoration of degraded land
UNDP: With UNDP support, Ladakh declared 'Yaya Tso' a high-altitude lake, covering an area of more than 6,600 hectares, the 1st biodiversity heritage site at a high-altitude lake and designating the Hanley village cluster, including the wetland complex, covering 1,00,000 hectares as India's first Night Sky Reserve . Through soil and moisture conservation activities undertaken; and the biodigesters installed in the Kanchendzonga Biosphere Reserve in the State of Sikkim has helped protect and restore 10,000 hectares  of snow leopard habitat

FAO: Under the GEF6 Green Ag project, landscape assessment, which includes geospatial analysis, secondary literature review, value chain analysis, community consultation, and household surveys which is a precursor to the development of Green Landscape Management Plans (GLMPs) has been completed in four landscapes. A curriculum for the Field School on Landscape Governance which has three modules, namely landscape delineation, livelihood and institutional support, and analysis developed for  the Green Landscape Management Plan (GLMP) in convergence with the government schemes and GEF funding.

Indicator: Reduction in plastic pollution
UNDP - The Plastic Waste Management (PWM) programme demonstrated its impact by facilitating the collection and processing of 6,988.78 of plastic waste and 2,206.48 of dry waste until November 2023. This effort prevented the release of over 22,047 MTs of CO2 emissions by channelizing plastic waste away from landfills to recycling. In the year 2023, the project was operational in 4 cities in 4 states across the country.

Indicator: Area under sustainable agriculture
FAO: Under the GEF6 Green Ag project, Field schools were conducted with the village-level committees in Madhya Pradesh, Mizoram, Odisha and Uttarakhand. Curricula for farmer field schools (FFS) on sustainable agriculture and livestock management developed and implemented in four landscapes in Madhya Pradesh, Mizoram, Odisha and Uttarakhand.

WFP: WFP aims to strengthen the adaptive capacity of the government, civil society groups and communities against climatic stressors and build climate-resilient livelihoods and food systems for sustainable food and nutrition security. To achieve this objective, WFP is implementing several pilot projects to demonstrate and operationalize the use of innovative technologies at the grass-roots level, empower communities through community-based planning, and support livelihood diversification.

UNWOMEN: Under the Carbon Offsetting Rice Emission (CORE) program 3955 smallholder women farmers capacities were develped on sustaibale rice production measures with emission reduction using gender inclusive approaches in the districts of Mandla and Balaghat in Madhya Pradesh and Jind in Haryana. Train the Trainer modules on gender created and trainings organised for master trianers as well as consotrum partners. 
The project is ongoing and the target is to be achieved by December 2025.

Indicator:
The UN, led by UNICEF, provided technical assistance, wide-ranging capacity building, and promotion of safe practices to improve Water and Sanitation (WASH) services in India. 2023 saw India make significant progress in the provision of safely managed water supply and sanitation services, reaching 124 million and 17.3 million people, respectively. 
500,000 villages are now reported to have achieved Open Defecation Free plus status (ODF+) by not only maintaining ODF status but also implementing robust solid and liquid waste management systems and ensuring a clean environment for children. 
UNICEF support for Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) campaign contributed to the mobilization of over 1 million people and to 1,280,766 community engagement activities across India for ODF+. Films developed for SHS played in cinema halls (9,300 screens) across India.
A total of 933 healthcare facilities gained access to sustainable WASH services and a further 168,340 schools implemented climate-smart clean and green school improvement plans including menstrual hygiene management services to ensure girl-friendly school environments in target states.
As the Government of India significantly expanded the provision of WASH services through the national water and sanitation flagship programmes, UNICEF strategically scaled up its policy engagement and technical support on monitoring and quality assurance for sustainable implementation of WASH action plans. Technical support focused on the development of implementation guidelines and training of implementing partners at various levels as well as community engagement for sustained behavioural change and professionalization of water and sanitation workers at community level for sustainability. 
UNICEF also played a more strategic role in strengthening WASH results monitoring in line with SDG/Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP) indicators, by facilitating consultations with multiple Ministries and the global WHO/ UNICEF JMP team. This engagement gave UNICEF the opportunity to expand its evidence-based engagement and strategic guidance, as well as strengthen monitoring of WASH results for children, including the most vulnerable in hard-to-reach communities.
